anchor.surface_text: The Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Guntur Tobaccos Ltd. 2  this Court pointed out  at p. 255  A companytract for work in the execution of which goods are used may take one of three forms.

precedents.case_name: Government of Andhra Pradesh v Guntur Tobaccos Ltd
precedents.cited_proposition: A contract for work in the execution of which goods are used may take one of three forms. The contract may be for work to be done for remuneration and for supply of materials used in the execution of the works for a price; it may be a contract for work in which the use of materials is accessory or incidental to the execution of the work; or it may be a contract for work and use or supply of materials though not accessory to the execution of the contract is voluntary or gratuitous. Whether a contract is of the first or the second class must depend upon the circumstances; if it is of the first, it is a composite contract for work and sale of goods; where it is of the second category, it is a contract for execution of work not involving sale of goods
